name: Weighted Pull-Up

instructions.setup: Attach a dip belt with weight around your waist. Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
execution: Initiate the pull by driving your elbows down towards your hips.
Pull your body up until your chin clears the bar.
Lower yourself under control to a full dead hang.
tips: Keep your core tight and legs straight or slightly crossed.
Avoid using momentum or swinging.
Focus on depressing your scapula before pulling.

description: An advanced progression of the standard pull-up designed to maximize lat hypertrophy and pulling strength by introducing external resistance.

name: Barbell Overhead Press

instructions.setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Grip the bar just outside your shoulders, resting it on your front delts.
execution: Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Press the bar vertically in a straight line, moving your head back slightly to clear the path.
Lock out at the top with the bar directly over your mid-foot.
Lower the bar back to the starting position under control.
tips: Do not use leg drive (that would be a Push Press).
Keep your elbows slightly in front of the bar at the start.
Do not hyperextend your lower back.

description: A fundamental strength exercise for the shoulders and upper body stability.

name: Weighted Chest Dips

instructions.setup: Secure weight with a dip belt. Mount the parallel bars with arms locked out and shoulders depressed.
execution: Lean forward slightly (approx 30 degrees) to target the chest.
Lower your body until your shoulders are slightly below your elbows.
Press back up to the starting position, extending the elbows.
tips: Keep your elbows tucked in, don't let them flare out excessively.
Control the descent to protect your shoulders.
Maintain the forward lean throughout the movement.

description: Effective for building chest and triceps. Lean forward to emphasize the chest.

name: Cable Face Pulls

instructions.setup: Set a cable pulley to face height with a rope attachment. Grasp the rope with thumbs facing backward (neutral grip).
execution: Pull the rope towards your forehead, separating your hands as you pull.
Externally rotate your shoulders at the end range (thumbs pointing back).
Squeeze your rear delts and upper back.
Return to start with control.
tips: Focus on pulling with your elbows and rear delts, not your biceps.
This is a postural health exercise, prioritize form over heavy weight.
Keep your chest up and core braced.

description: Excellent for shoulder health and posture. Pull towards the forehead.

name: Barbell Back Squat

instructions.setup: Place the barbell on your upper back (traps). Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
execution: Take a deep breath and brace your core.
Initiate by breaking at the hips and knees simultaneously.
Lower until your hip crease is below your knee (parallel).
Drive through your heels to return to the standing position.
tips: Keep your chest up and spine neutral.
Track your knees over your toes.
Do not let your knees cave inward.

description: The king of lower body exercises. Targets quads, glutes, and overall strength.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift

instructions.setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding dumbbells/barbell in front of your thighs.
execution: Unlock your knees slightly (do not squat).
Push your hips back as far as possible, keeping the weight close to your legs.
Lower until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings.
Squeeze your glutes to drive your hips forward and return to the start.
tips: Keep your spine neutral (flat back) throughout.
Think about 'closing a car door with your butt'.
Do not go lower if your back starts to round.

description: Focuses on the posterior chain. Hinge at the hips and feel the stretch.

name: Dead Bug

instructions.setup: Lie on your back with arms extended towards the ceiling and legs in a tabletop position (knees bent at 90 degrees).
execution: Press your lower back into the floor (flatten the curve).
Slowly lower opposite arm and leg towards the floor.
Exhale as you lower, inhaling as you return to start.
Repeat on the other side.
tips: The most important part is keeping your lower back glued to the floor.
Do not let your ribs flare up.
Move slowly and with control.

description: A core stability exercise that teaches you to move your limbs while maintaining a neutral spine.

name: Incline Treadmill Walk
description: Low-intensity steady-state cardio. Great for recovery and heart health.

name: Incline Dumbbell Bench Press

instructions.setup: Set the bench to a 30-45 degree incline. Kick the dumbbells up to your shoulders using your knees.
execution: Retract your shoulder blades and puff your chest out.
Press the dumbbells up and slightly inward (but don't bang them together).
Lower the weights slowly until you feel a deep stretch in your upper chest.
tips: Do not flare your elbows out 90 degrees; keep them around 45 degrees.
Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows.
Maintain contact with the bench with your head, upper back, and glutes.

description: Targets the upper pectoral muscles using dumbbells for a greater range of motion.

name: Chest Supported Row

instructions.setup: Set an incline bench to around 45 degrees. Lie face down with a dumbbell in each hand.
execution: Pull the weights towards your hips, retracting your shoulder blades.
Squeeze your back hard at the top.
Lower the weights fully to a stretched position.
tips: Keep your chest pressed against the pad at all times.
Do not use momentum to jerk the weight up.

description: A rowing variation that isolates the back by removing the need for lower body stability.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise

instructions.setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding dumbbells at your sides. Lean forward very slightly.
execution: Raise the weights out to the sides, leading with your elbows.
Stop when your arms are parallel to the floor.
Lower the weights back down with control, stopping just before they touch your body to keep tension.
tips: Imagine you are pouring water out of a pitcher at the top.
Do not use momentum or swing your torso.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows.

description: The primary exercise for isolating the lateral head of the deltoids for shoulder width.

name: Diamond Push-Up

instructions.setup: Get into a push-up position with your hands close together, index fingers and thumbs touching to form a diamond.
execution: Lower your chest towards your hands, keeping elbows tucked close to your body.
Touch your chest to your hands (or go as low as comfortable).
Push back up to full lockout.
tips: Engage your core to prevent your hips from sagging.
Focus on squeezing your triceps at the top.
If it hurts your wrists, widen your hands slightly.

description: A push-up variation with hands close together to heavily emphasize the triceps.
